account: For x=3, the equation becomes (y-6)(z-6)=36; the ordered positive divisor pairs (1,36),(2,18),(3,12),(4,9),(6,6) give exactly (3,7,42),(3,8,24),(3,9,18),(3,10,15),(3,12,12). For x=4, the equation becomes (y-4)(z-4)=16; the ordered positive divisor pairs (1,16),(2,8),(4,4) give exactly (4,5,20),(4,6,12),(4,8,8). Every listed triple is verified by common-denominator substitution to sum to 1/2, and the factor-pair enumeration proves completeness within each fixed-x case.
assumptions: All variables are positive integers and solutions are normalized by x <= y <= z.
For fixed x=3, the condition 1/y+1/z=1/6 forces y,z > 6, so the factors y-6 and z-6 are positive; for fixed x=4, y,z > 4, so y-4 and z-4 are positive.
Divisor enumeration uses only positive ordered divisor pairs with the smaller factor first, matching y <= z.
Substitution checks use exact common-denominator rational arithmetic.
